settings.heading: The reasons brands call us
settings.subcopy: Six sentences we hear on almost every first call, and what we do about each one.

settings.pain: My agency ships slowly and I never see progress.
settings.answer: Fixed scope, two-week increments, and a staging URL you can open any day of the week.

settings.pain: The app works but nobody uses it.
settings.answer: Usually a product problem, not an engineering one. We start at flows and instrumentation, not features.

settings.pain: My site looks fine and converts badly.
settings.answer: Conversion work on the pages that carry traffic, copy, speed, creative and checkout, measured properly.

settings.pain: My creative looks cheap next to competitors.
settings.answer: Brand, packaging, product imagery and 3D produced in-house, no three-week wait for a revision.

settings.pain: Amazon eats my margin and I can't see why.
settings.answer: Campaign structure rebuilt around contribution profit, plus listing and catalog work that stops the leak upstream.

settings.pain: I have five vendors and nobody owns the number.
settings.answer: One team across build, creative and growth. One report, one person accountable for the outcome.

settings.heading: The questions you were going to ask anyway
settings.subcopy: If yours isn't here, ask it on the form, we answer every one.

settings.question: What does a project cost?
settings.answer: Discovery is a fixed, small fee. After it you get a scope and a number for the build, not a range that moves. Ongoing growth work runs monthly. We'd rather lose a deal on price than surprise you halfway through one.

settings.question: How long does a build take?
settings.answer: A marketing site or Shopify storefront: 4â€“8 weeks. A mobile app or web application: 12â€“20 weeks to a first release, depending on scope. Anyone quoting faster without seeing your requirements is guessing.

settings.question: Do I have to use you for both build and growth?
settings.answer: No. Plenty of clients use one side only. The reason we offer both is that the handoff between a dev shop and a marketing agency is where most projects lose a quarter.

settings.question: Who owns the code and the accounts?
settings.answer: You do, repositories, ad accounts, analytics, everything. We work inside your accounts where possible and hand over cleanly if you ever leave.

settings.question: Do you work with early-stage companies?
settings.answer: Yes, when the scope is real. We'd rather build a sharp first version than a full platform for an idea that hasn't met a customer.

settings.question: What happens after launch?
settings.answer: Either you take it in-house with documentation and a handover session, or we stay on a support and growth retainer. Both are normal; neither is locked in.
